label: Tutorial: Rules Explorer
description: Steps of the Tutorial button on the Rules Explorer page (endpoint rule.rules_list). A step: target (CSS selector, empty = centred card), title, text (blank line = new paragraph, **bold**, `code`), roles (optional: anonymous, user, member, admin, perm:<key>), demo (rule / bundle: example shown when the target is missing, e.g. an empty list).

steps.title: Every rule in one place
steps.text: All public rules of this instance, whatever their format. This tour goes through the search, every filter and what a rule card tells you.

steps.title: Search
steps.text: Type words, a rule name, a CVE or a technique id. The search runs on the field chosen in the filters (all fields by default) and the list updates as you type.

steps.title: Sort
steps.text: Newest, recently updated, most liked, best quality… the order of the cards.

steps.title: Cards or table
steps.text: Cards show a preview of each rule. The table shows more rules at once: the column picker next to it chooses which columns to show.

steps.title: Filters
steps.text: Opens the filter box. The number on the button is how many filters are active. Every filter is kept in the address of the page: copy it and others see the same list.

steps.title: The filter box
steps.text: Narrow the list down by **format**, **quality score**, **source**, **CVE**, **ATT&CK technique**, **licence**, **tags**, **author** and **risk level**, plus quick switches (only rules with a CVE, with tags, mapped to ATT&CK…). Once a filter is set, export the result or turn it into a bundle.

steps.title: Format and quick options
steps.text:
**Format**: only YARA, Sigma, Suricata…

**Search in**: where the search box looks (title, description, content, author…).

The switches keep only rules that: match exactly, are linked to other rules, have a CVE, have tags, have a real licence, are mapped to ATT&CK.

steps.title: Quality score
steps.text: Keep only rules whose quality score (0 to 100) is in this range — e.g. 70 to 100 for the best ones.

steps.title: Sources
steps.text: Where the rules come from: a Git repository, an import, a file. Pick one or several.

steps.title: Vulnerabilities
steps.text: Rules that detect given CVEs or GHSA ids.

steps.title: ATT&CK techniques
steps.text: Rules mapped to given MITRE ATT&CK techniques (T1059, Command and Scripting Interpreter…).

steps.title: Licences
steps.text: Only rules under the licences you can use (MIT, DRL, GPL…).

steps.title: Tags
steps.text: Malware families, platforms, TLP / PAP levels, threat actors… Several tags = rules having all of them.

steps.title: Author or editor
steps.text: Rules written by someone, or published by a given Rulezet user.

steps.title: Risk level
steps.text: The risk level computed for each rule (how likely it is to be noisy or dangerous to deploy).

steps.title: Take the result
steps.text: Once a filter is set: export the matching rules or turn them into a bundle in one click.

steps.title: Alert me
steps.text: Turn the current filters into an alert: you get a notification each time a new rule matches them.

steps.title: A rule card
steps.text: One card per rule. Click its title to open the rule; the parts of the card follow.

steps.title: Badges
steps.text: Format, version and quality of the rule at a glance.

steps.title: Title, author and date
steps.text: Who published it and when it last changed.

steps.title: Description
steps.text: What the rule detects, in the author's words.

steps.title: CVEs
steps.text: Vulnerabilities this rule detects — click one to open its response kit.

steps.title: ATT&CK
steps.text: Techniques this rule detects — click one to see every rule for it.

steps.title: Tags
steps.text: Click a tag to filter the list on it.

steps.title: Details
steps.text: Source, licence and other details of the rule.

steps.title: Votes
steps.text: What the community thinks of the rule. Logged-in users can vote.

steps.title: Peek at the rule
steps.text: Shows the rule's content right in the list, without opening it.

steps.title: Favorite
steps.text: Keeps the rule in your favorites (your account page).

steps.title: More actions
steps.text: Download, copy, add to a bundle, report…
